I know that I will catch hell for saying this, but I am pretty happy with the 14in Alienware laptop that I got.

Now before I am skewered,

  • I got it 3 years ago, and the battery life has not dropped (I'll admit that it was never above 2~2.5 hours anyway)

  • The SSD keeps the booting time low

  • It still runs modern games at 60 with decent graphics settings.

  • The keyboard is amazing, but that may be personal preference.

  • as a developer as well, everything works fine.

  • I have dropped it a couple of times, the screen still works, the hdd has not failed, the case dented the ground, and the speakers still sound good.

If you want something more practical. I really enjoy the surfaces. They appear to be gimmicky, but they can handle quite a bit unless you need to be running 4 virtual machines (sticking with my alienware for that). They are quite solid little tablet/laptop things.

I had a Dell Inspiron from around 2003-2009. It was great, and it lasted all that time, even through a combat zone, keyboard replacement, upgrades, etc. Eventually, though, it just couldn't take it anymore and died. So, I started researching.

I decided early on that I wanted a convertible tablet/laptop because I teach and I thought it would be useful. That narrowed it down a bit. After a lot of research, I decided on the Fujitsu T902. Expensive, but I found that Fujitsu sells refurbs on eBay and you can save thousands of dollars. So, I started watching the auctions and bids. Eventually, I found a T902 with the specs I wanted (i5, 2gb RAM, 500gb HDD) at the right time, and managed to get it for about $1,000 (Approximately $3,000 if configured on Fujitsu's website). With the saved money, I upgraded the RAM, put in an SSD, and bought a spare charger.

It has been the most dependable, fastest, nicest laptop I've ever owned or used. I have ZERO regrets. It looks nice, it works very well, and I've never had a problem with it. I would buy a T904 in a heartbeat.

It is not that great for gaming - it has onboard graphics, so you can't play Skyrim, but it works fine with platformers and simpler games. I never game much on it - maybe some pokerstars or something - because I use it mainly for work. I love it, and I"ll buy another Fujitsu when it dies.

tl,dr: Fujitsu is an awesome brand. As with any laptop, upgrade to SSD/more RAM, and do a clean install to get ride of bloatware.
